claims.summary: read_generation enforces uid()==0, mode 0o444, nlink()==1, rejects symlinks, and caps the file at 256 bytes.
claims.disposition: Verified against complete report-time source. maintenance.rs:516-523 checks !is_file, is_symlink, nlink()!=1, uid()!=0, permissions().mode()&0o777!=0o444 and len()>256, bailing with 'generation binding identity failed'. Every structural constraint she names is present and exact; the 256-byte cap she does not name is an additional constraint on the same gate.

claims.summary: read_generation omits the runtime_gid check that ScheduledReflection requires.
claims.disposition: Verified. read_generation's signature is (path: &Path) — runtime_gid never enters its scope. The identifier appears at exactly 8 sites: the Paths field (123), getegid() init (282), two call-sites passing it into read_bound_lease for BOTH lease kinds (308, 314), the read_bound_lease param/forward (339, 341), the read_bound_lease_for_owner param (349), and one single comparison (365).

claims.summary: read_bound_lease_for_owner explicitly requires metadata.gid() == runtime_gid for ScheduledReflection, in the match block she cites at 362-367.
claims.disposition: Verified with a one-line offset on each side: the match on kind runs 362-366, the GenerationTransition arm is 363 (mode 0o444 only) and the ScheduledReflection arm 364-366 (mode 0o440 AND metadata.gid() != runtime_gid). The mechanism she names is exact; only the cited span is slightly wide. Both arms sit inside the same fail-closed bail at 367-369.

Contradicted as a call, confirmed as a predicate. read_generation contains no call to valid_identifier; 528-541 INLINES the same rule (non-empty, len<=128, not '.'/'..', [A-Za-z0-9] plus '.','_','-' after index 0) and adds a stricter canonical form at 541: bytes must equal "{generation}\n". valid_identifier (548-558) is called exactly once in this file, at 456, on the reflection lease's generation_id.

claims.summary: GenerationTransition relies on 0o444 while ScheduledReflection uses a stricter identity gate.
claims.disposition: Verified for both surfaces. The transition LEASE requires mode 0o444 (363) and the generation BINDING likewise 0o444 (521); the reflection lease requires 0o440 plus the group match (365). The reflection path additionally binds host_boot_id, service_invocation_id, generation_id, an exact 3h lifetime (446-456) and a generation equality check in write_ack (481-487) that the transition path does not carry.

claims.summary: Hypothesis: a GenerationTransition is a global structural state change, so 'who' (GID) is implicitly covered by 'how' (root ownership and strict mode).
claims.disposition: Recorded as her hypothesis, not confirmed as intent. Complete source read: maintenance.rs states no rationale for the asymmetry — the only explanatory comments are the fail-closed notes at 119-121 and 244-245. The structural facts are consistent with her reading (root-owned 0o444 with nlink==1 and O_NOFOLLOW reads), but nothing in the file records why the GID was omitted, so intent stays unestablished.

claims.summary: Hypothesis: ScheduledReflection is a higher-risk, granular action, so runtime_gid acts as a secondary key against a root-level non-kernel-group entity.
claims.disposition: Recorded as hypothesis; partly corroborated, not ranked. Source shows the reflection path is strictly more constrained (0o440 + gid, boot-id equality, fixed 3h window, lease-generation equality at 481-487). It does NOT rank the two kinds by risk, and the gid check is an effective-GID comparison from getegid() (282), so it distinguishes runtime group, not privilege level. No risk ordering is inferred here.

claims.summary: STUDY_QUESTION: is runtime_gid ever used inside read_generation or other transition-related functions, or strictly reserved for ScheduledReflection and BoundLease?
claims.disposition: Answered from complete source and pinned by a new regression. The GID is SHARED as a parameter on both lease paths (308, 314) but COMPARED at exactly one site, the ScheduledReflection arm (365). read_generation, validate_transition_lease, write_ack, stable_read and atomic_owner_write never consult it; ACK-side protection is mode-based instead (parent &0o077==0, file 0o600). New test: generation_transition_lease_ignores_the_runtime_group.
